description: Occupancy-token backstop in the orchestrator recycle watcher: force a recycle when the current context occupancy of the last request exceeds a fraction of the model window, avoiding silent auto-compaction on a pathologically long cycle.

userStories.title: Add parseContextOccupancy primitive (last-request occupancy, not cumulative)
userStories.description: As the recycle watcher, I need a pure primitive that reports the CURRENT context occupancy of the orchestrator (input+cache tokens of the LAST request in the transcript) so that a backstop can compare live window usage against a ceiling without mistaking cumulative cross-request traffic for context size.
acceptanceCriteria: A new exported function parseContextOccupancy lives in src/transcript/usage.ts and returns the occupancy of the LAST usage-bearing request = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens of the final request in the JSONL (output_tokens excluded). [oracle: grep -q 'export function parseContextOccupancy' src/transcript/usage.ts]

A test proves occupancy is NOT cumulative: on a multi-request fake transcript (>= 3 requests with growing input), parseContextOccupancy returns only the last request's input+cache and is strictly less than the cumulative parseTranscriptUsage(input+cacheCreation+cacheRead). [oracle: bun test test/transcript/usage.test.ts]

The occupancy value equals the last request's tokens exactly (a request whose usage lines are duplicated per content block is counted once, matching the last usage payload seen). [oracle: bun test test/transcript/usage.test.ts]
parseContextOccupancy does not delegate to parseTranscriptUsage/computeOrchBudget for its return value (occupancy is last-request, never a cumulative sum). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all), no --no-verify. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: File: src/transcript/usage.ts (add export next to parseTranscriptUsage); test: test/transcript/usage.test.ts. CRITICAL (journal.md:468-469, CAM-23 misfire): parseTranscriptUsage sums cumulative traffic (~5.58M/session real) by deduping (message.id, requestId) across ALL requests; occupancy must instead take the LAST usage-bearing line's payload only. TranscriptUsage/MessageUsage interfaces already exist in this file; reuse the JSONL split + JSON.parse + isTranscriptLine guards. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: getting lines[lines.length-1] is T|undefined, guard it. Return 0 for empty/no-usage transcripts. Do NOT include output_tokens (occupancy = input-window fill only).

userStories.title: Add model->context-window mapping, backstop fraction, and over-backstop decision
userStories.description: As the recycle watcher, I need a named constant for the orchestrator model's context window (keyed to the configured orchestrator model) plus a named backstop fraction and a pure over-threshold decision, so the backstop compares occupancy against a real window ceiling rather than a bare literal.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/orchestrator/context-window.ts exports a named Opus window constant (e.g. OPUS_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 200_000) and ORCH_CONTEXT_BACKSTOP_FRACTION (~0.8). [oracle: grep -Eq 'OPUS_CONTEXT_WINDOW|ORCH_CONTEXT_BACKSTOP_FRACTION' src/orchestrator/context-window.ts]

orchestratorContextWindow(configPath?) resolves the window by keying readPhaseModel('orchestrator') to the model->window mapping; an unknown/absent model falls back to the default window (never throws, mirroring the defensive readPhaseModel contract). [oracle: grep -q "readPhaseModel('orchestrator'" src/orchestrator/context-window.ts]

A pure isOverContextBackstop(occupancy, window, fraction) returns true iff occupancy > window * fraction, with a test covering the boundary (== is not over, > is over) and the default-fraction path. [oracle: bun test test/orchestrator/context-window.test.ts]
The module does not import or reuse computeOrchBudget/parseTranscriptUsage (no cumulative spend leaks into the window/backstop logic). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all), no --no-verify. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file: src/orchestrator/context-window.ts; test: test/orchestrator/context-window.test.ts. Reads model via readPhaseModel('orchestrator', configPath) from src/config/models.ts (default 'claude-opus-4-8'). No model->window mapping exists in the codebase today (src/orchestrator/budget.ts has none; grep contextWindow/200000 in src/ returns nothing) -- introduce it here as a NAMED constant, never a bare literal at the call site. Opus context window = 200_000 (established Claude Opus 4.x fact). Sonnet is also 200k today, so a small keyed mapping with a 200k default is sufficient; keep it defensive (unknown model -> default window). ORCH_CONTEXT_BACKSTOP_FRACTION default ~0.8 (no operator override in scope). Keep this module a pure config/decision layer so US-003 only wires it.

userStories.title: Wire occupancy backstop into the recycle watcher tick (arm marker when over ceiling)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator lifecycle, I need the recycle watcher to force a recycle when the orchestrator's current context occupancy crosses the backstop ceiling, by arming the same CAM-162 recycle marker, so a pathologically long cycle recycles deterministically instead of hitting silent auto-compaction.
acceptanceCriteria: The watcher (src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts) computes the orchestrator's current context occupancy each poll tick (reads the orchestrator transcript, applies parseContextOccupancy) and arms ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER (writes the empty marker file) when occupancy > ORCH_CONTEXT_BACKSTOP_FRACTION * orchestratorContextWindow. [oracle: grep -q 'parseContextOccupancy' src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts]

A test with an injected high-occupancy reader drives one tick that arms the marker and fires SIGTERM on the resolved PID; a low-occupancy reader drives a tick that arms no marker and sends no signal (killFn not called). [oracle: bun test test/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]

The backstop reuses the CAM-162 signal path: it arms ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER (never a new marker) so the existing marker-consume + SIGTERM logic fires; the marker-arming is done via an injectable seam (default writes .claude/<ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER>). [oracle: grep -q 'ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER' src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts]

The backstop uses the default fraction (ORCH_CONTEXT_BACKSTOP_FRACTION) with no operator-set number; a missing/empty orchestrator transcript yields no occupancy reading and no-op (never a false-positive recycle). [oracle: bun test test/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]
The watcher registers no --permission-mode flag (invariant preserved). [oracle: bun test test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

userStories.notes: File: src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts (extend OrchRecycleWatchOptions + the tick); test: test/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts (unit with injected deps; the existing real-process proof lives in test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts, do not regress it). Add injectable seams: readOccupancyFn (prod: read orchestratorTranscriptPath(cwd, claudeDir) from src/transcript/usage.ts + parseContextOccupancy; null when transcript absent), armMarkerFn (prod: writeFileSync(join(claudeDir, ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER), '', 'utf8') -- mirror index.ts:1181), plus contextWindow + backstopFraction (prod: orchestratorContextWindow() + ORCH_CONTEXT_BACKSTOP_FRACTION from US-002). In the tick: check backstop FIRST (if over, armMarkerFn), THEN run existing handleOneTick so the armed marker drives SIGTERM+consume-once through one unified path. Watcher cwd is the project root (spawned by run.ts:549), so readPhaseModel's default project.toml path resolves; no run.ts change needed (deps are built inside runOrchRecycleWatch). OUT OF SCOPE: the recycle/respawn/rehydrate mechanism itself (CAM-162); a backstop firing without a fresh handoff cold-boots on respawn, which is CAM-162 cold-start-safe behavior. Keep biome cognitive-complexity under 15 (extract a checkBackstop helper if needed, CAM-60 pattern). No templates/ touch, so no vendor re-embed.
